scope: Virtual Key emergency revocation propagation from Control Plane to independent Data Plane

environment.provider: none; synthetic model intentionally has no route/deployment

procedure: Issue one environment-bound PROVIDER Virtual Key in the real Access & Keys UI; keep the one-time secret in process memory only.
Send a valid synthetic no-route completion request to Data Plane 18152.
Use the real UI Actions > Revoke key > Revoke (graceful drain) workflow on the Control Plane.
Replay the same key on independent Data Plane 18153 and read back key metadata from the UI/API.

before_revocation.meaning: authentication/admission passed; no upstream route existed, so no provider dispatch occurred

after_revocation.meaning: independent Data Plane rejected replay after Control Plane revocation

visual_inspection: Access & Keys visibly reports the tested key as Revoked and the revocation success notice. The screenshot contains only metadata, never the one-time plaintext.
limitations: One key, two Data Planes, one orderly graceful revocation, one replay.

Sub-second propagation bound, active stream severance, concurrent request race, Valkey outage/failover, PostgreSQL notification fallback, multiple tenants/roles, and production multi-host networking remain unverified.
